quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: To turn left, press the left handgrip. This makes the motorcycle lean in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: How can you discourage another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This makes it harder for other drivers to share your lane.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Cross angled railroad tracks while riding straight in your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you might end up in another lane.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than they are during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it difficult to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use your high beam when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The horn button is usually next to the left handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: If you are transporting a passenger, they should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you through turns. They should sit as far forward as possible without getting in your way. They should hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering are warning signs. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
Don't help to improve a rider's visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
questions.explanation: Choose a bright helmet color. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Allow the other driver to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make it more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: Successful motorcycle riders know they are safest when they are:

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seen by other motorists.
questions.explanation: Successful motorcycle riders know they are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and lane position to make yourself more visible.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position your motorcycle in the lane so other drivers will see you as soon as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to be farther from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more noticeable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle in the lane so other drivers will see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you earliest. For example, when a blind corner is to your right, stay on the left side of your lane instead of the center so drivers can see you sooner.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders who are inexperienced on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who are inexperienced on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who do not have much experience riding their motorcycle.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Rely only on mirrors to see other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Slam on the brakes to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic behind you before changing lanes.

questions.question: Drivers entering from a ramp may not see you on the highway. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Weave in your lane to be more obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, give merging vehicles plenty of space to safely enter traffic. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can do so safely. If no other lane is available, slow down to give the merging driver more space.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks up while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it again with a smooth motion.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Adjust them so you can see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels lose grip on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, your wheels may lose grip on the road and you could crash.

questions.question: How should you usually handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up increases danger because they may tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: About the front brake:

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is less effective than the rear brake.
It is safe to use if used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, and it is safe to use when used properly.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle during a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
